{{c|{{xx-larger|THE ACTES OF THE}}}}
{{c|{{x-larger|APOSTLES.}}}}

{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The}} 1. part. The expectation of the Holy Ghost between the Ascension of Christ, and the beginning of the Church.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. I.}}}}}}

{{c|''Christ now ready to ascend, biddeth the Apostles to expect the Holy Ghost which he had promised, foretelling where (being strengthened by him) they should begin his Church, and hovv far they should cary it. 9 After his Ascension they are warned by two Angels to set their mindes vpon his second comming. 14 In the daies of their expectation, 15 Peter beginneth to execute his vicarship, giuing instruction and order, by vvhich Mathias is elected Apostle in the place of Iudas.''}} {{dropinitial|T|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial T, an urn and foliage.png|imgsize=205px|fl={{verse|chapter=1|verse=1}}}}HE {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 1, 3.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle at Masse vpon Ascension day.}}first treatise I made of {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Not al particularly, (for the other Euangelists write diuers thinges not touched by him) but al the principal and most necessarie thinges.}}∷ al things, O Theophilus, which {{sc|Iesvs}} began to doe and to teache, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=2}}† vntil the day vvherein {{sup|‖}} giuing commaundement by the holy Ghost to the Apostles vvhom he chose, he vvas assumpted: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=3}}† to whom he shewed also him self aliue after his passion in many arguments, for fourtie daies appearing to them, & speaking of the kingdom of God. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=4}}† And eating vvith them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 24, 49.''}}* he commaunded them, that they should not depart from Hierusalem, but should expect the promisse of the Father, vvhich you {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 14, 26.''}}* haue heard (saith he) by my mouth: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=5}}† for Iohn in deede baptized vvith {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 3, 16.''}}* vvater, but {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Iohns Baptisme gaue not the Holy Ghost.}}∷ you shal be {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The aboundant powring of the Holy Ghost vpon them on Whitsunday, he calleth baptisme.}}∷ baptized vvith the holy Ghost after these fevv daies. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=6}}† They therfore that vvere assembled, asked him, saying, Lord, whether at this time vvilt thou restore the kingdom to Israel? {{verse|chapter=1|verse=7}}† but he said to them, {{sup|‖}} It is not for you to know times or moments, vvhich the Father hath put in his owne power: {{verse|chapter=1|verse=8}}† but you shal receiue the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 24, 49. Act. 2, 1.''}}* vertue of the holy Ghost comming vpon you, and you shal be witnesses vnto me in Hierusalem, and in al Iewrie, and Samaria, and euen to the vtmost of the earth. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=9}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 16, 19. Lu. 24, 51.''}}* vvhen he had said these things, in their sight he vvas eleuated: and a cloud receiued him out of their sight. {{verse|chapter=1|verse=10}}† And vvhen they beheld him going into heauen, behold two men stoode beside them in white garments, {{verse|chapter=1|verse=11}}† vvho also said, Ye men of Galilee, vvhy<noinclude>{{rh||Oo|stand}}</noinclude>
